transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-07-23
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Tom Reynolds (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood CSM), Nate Barlow (SilverCove CTO), Maya Chen (DevOps), Ravi Patel (Product), Sam Ortiz (Security), Asha (SRE)

Auto-generated Summary: Quick kickoff to scope production activation, network/VPC intake, security requirements (SOC2/KMS), and initial runtime sizing. Agreed to share docs and schedule private deployment walkthrough.

Topics: onboarding runbook; VPC & peering; KMS & key management; Dedicated vs Hosted; latency/cost expectations; pilot success criteria; timelines

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for, uh, taking the time. I'm Priya from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:06] Nate: Nate Barlow, CTO at SilverCove. Hey.
[00:08] Maya: Maya, DevOps. Good to meet you all.
[00:11] Ravi: Ravi, Product. Excited to get rolling.
[00:13] Sam: Sam, security. I'll be listening for compliance bits.
[00:15] Priya: Great. Tom and Lena from our side as well. Today's goal: make sure we map the runbook, capture network and security needs, and align on pilot success metrics and timing.
[00:29] Tom: I'll cover technical intake — runtime sizing, seq length expectations, and perf tradeoffs. A couple clarifying q's up front: are you expecting mostly short prompts or long-context chains?
[00:38] Asha: Majority are short, two to three shot prompts, but we have a subset of support-case summarization that needs ~2k tokens occasionally.
[00:45] Tom: okay, that's helpful — so mixed workloads. That affects caching and kv usage, and also batch sizes.
[00:52] Priya: Quick note on timelines — what's your target for pilot / canary?
[00:58] Nate: We want a pilot by mid-August, ideally ramping to limited prod by end of Q3. But security signoff is a gating item.
[01:07] Priya: Understood. We'll line up the security docs. Sam, can you share the main certs?
[01:12] Sam: SOC2 is a must, and we need KMS support for customer keys, plus audit logs retention policy. Also SSO/SAML for admin access.
[01:21] Lena: We have an enterprise package that supports SSO/SAML, and you can choose customer-managed KMS when deploying Private. I'll attach the integration guide.
[01:29] Maya: For networking, we prefer a VPC peering option over public egress. Do you support VPC peering and restricted egress?
[01:36] Tom: Yes — both VPC peering and private deployments (VPC or on-prem) are supported. For hosted, we can do VPC egress endpoints and IP allowlists. There may be a small config caveat around cross-account roles, but it's standard.
[01:50] Ravi: On model side — we're evaluating both open models and a couple of fine-tuned variants. Cost is a real constraint; we need predictable per-token economics.
[01:59] Tom: We can recommend quantization and batching profiles to reduce unit cost; for the 2k token workloads we'll likely suggest a dedicated pool to avoid latency spikes.
[02:09] Sam: What about data residency? Some of our clients require EU-only processing for certain workloads.
[02:14] Priya: We have region pins and private deployments to meet residency. For Hosted, you can pin to our EU region; Private gives full control. We'll send the region availability matrix.
[02:23] Maya: For the network intake, what exact artifacts do you need? CIDR, firewall rules, peering keys?
[02:29] Tom: We'll need CIDR blocks, approved outbound ranges, proxy/load balancer details, and a contact for A/B testing of routes. If doing Private, SSH bastion and HSM/KMS endpoints.
[02:41] Asha: We use AWS with Transit Gateway; peering details will be similar to other vendors but let me circle back with exact TGW IDs.
[02:47] Priya: Perfect. I'll add that to action items.
[02:51] Tom: Quick perf note — for mixed short and long workloads, prefix caching (KV cache) can dramatically reduce repeated compute. But it's workload specific; we'll need sample prompts to tune.
[03:04] Ravi: We can share a representative prompt set and sample logs. Any constraints on sample data?
[03:10] Priya: Please scrub PII, but realistic examples are best. We'll treat them as ephemeral for tuning and can sign an NDA if needed.
[03:18] Sam: Also need retention policy details — how long do you keep logs and tokens?
[03:22] Lena: Default retention is 30 days for trial accounts; enterprise customers can extend or opt for logging offloading. We'll include the retention and audit log export options.
[03:33] Nate: Pricing — can you ballpark Dedicated monthly costs versus hosted per-token for our expected workload?
[03:40] Priya: We'll send an initial estimate based on the prompt set. Generally Dedicated is better if you have sustained throughput; hosted is cheaper for spiky low-volume. We'll provide a two-scenario estimate.
[03:52] Tom: For benchmarks, we recommend running a short perf test with our SE-runner — measures p99 latency, throughput at target batch sizes, and token cost. We can run this in Hosted dev first.
[04:05] Maya: How long does private deployment provisioning take? If we go Private with customer-managed KMS, what's the lead time?
[04:11] Priya: Typical on-prem or private VPC provisioning is 3-6 weeks depending on networking windows and compliance review. For cloud VPC private deployments it's often 2-4 weeks if networking is straightforward.
[04:21] Sam: Are there any known blockers with our KMS type? We're using AWS KMS with multi-account keys.
[04:27] Tom: AWS KMS works; we do need cross-account IAM roles or grant APIs set up. We can share a step-by-step. If you use HSM-backed keys, that adds a small integration step.
[04:40] Priya: Let's talk success criteria for the pilot — what defines a go/no-go?
[04:45] Ravi: Functionally, model quality within X% of our baseline on evaluation prompts. Operationally, p99 latency under 800ms for short prompts, and throughput for the support pipeline at 200 reqs/min. Security signoff done.
[04:58] Priya: Good — we'll map those to measurable dashboards. Lena: we'll set up per-route dashboards and alerting for regressions.
[05:06] Lena: And we can attach eval harness results to the CI pipeline so any model swap triggers alerts.
[05:13] Nate: One more thing — can we control model rollouts? We want canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallback to previous model on quality regression.
[05:23] Tom: Yes, Redwood supports rollout policies with automatic fallback. We'll document how to create a canary and tie regression tests.
[05:30] Maya: For the demo and next call, can Tom show a private deployment runbook and mapping to our TGW?
[05:36] Tom: Absolutely — I can do a 1-hr walkthrough. Proposed: 2027-07-29 16:00 UTC.
[05:44] Priya: Sounds good. We'll also send the onboarding checklist.
[05:48] (brief cross-talk)
[05:52] Sam: On logs — do you ship logs to customer S3 or do you keep them? Need export options.
[05:57] Lena: We support pushing logs to customer-owned S3 buckets, and you can integrate with SIEMs via our log forwarding. We'll include the S3 config steps.
[06:06] Nate: Any pitfalls others saw during initial deployments we should watch for?
[06:10] Tom: Common is underestimating warmup and KV cache sizing; also watch for sequence-length tail — if 1% of requests are very long, it can skew capacity. We'll show how to set autoscaling buffers.
[06:23] Asha: Is there a preferred quantization approach for AMD vs NVIDIA hardware?
[06:29] Tom: We have optimized kernels for both; quantization guidance depends on model and acceptable perp loss. We'll recommend profiles per model.
[06:38] Priya: Action items recap — I'll go through them now. Priya: send network and onboarding templates, Tom: schedule perf walkthrough 7/29, Lena: onboarding runbook, Maya: provide CIDR/TGW info, Sam: compliance checklist. Anything to add?
[06:53] Ravi: Please include sample pricing for dedicated monthly and per-token hosted estimates.
[06:56] Priya: Noted.
[06:58] (small pause)
[07:02] Nate: Great meeting. Look forward to the docs.
[07:05] Priya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[07:09] Lena: I'll set weekly 30-min touchpoints — propose Tuesdays.
[07:13] Maya: Tuesdays work.
[07:15] Priya: Alright, we'll close here — thanks team.

End of transcript.
